anti_overlap: Owns WHERE precomputation lives (source-side versus observer-side), the height→range closed form, per-query cost and per-answer byte size at dispatch time, and the edition/survey-date/invalidation discipline of the derived artefact including its participation in the identity hash. The kanyu lens owns the internal SHAPE of whatever is stored at a point — scalar versus angular horizon vector versus finite typology — and the directional content of that shape; this lens does not adjudicate record layout, and should take the per-point record as a parameter.

Both lenses will reach the vantage site and may reach opposite verdicts: this lens argues it as a charted mark with a height and an arc and asks whether that is rehabilitation or a relapse into fly-to-a-marker; the kanyu lens argues it as a configuration a point either has or does not. Each must argue in its own primitives rather than converging by borrowing.

On determinism, this lens frames the question as 'is the authority published, dated, and resolved identically by every reader' — provenance and versioning. The kanyu lens frames it as 'is the azimuth alphabet discrete and trig-free' — representation. Neither should re-litigate fixed-point arithmetic in general terms; both should cite fixed.rs for what actually exists.

The adversarial read of call 1 ('altitude is the fog's currency') is shared but split: this lens attacks it on cost asymmetry (the WHICH question is a cheap inequality, the HOW MUCH question is an expensive set, and the ruling picked the expensive one without pricing it); the kanyu lens attacks it on design substance (exposure versus enclosure, altitude as a monotone slider with no decision in it, and area-versus-detail as the real tradeoff).
decision_lens: Would a hydrographic office publish this as a Light List and a set of sailing directions — that is: is the visibility authority a FINITE, DATED, EDITIONED artefact that any two readers resolve identically, whose per-query answer is a bounded categorical or scalar lookup rather than a traverse of the city, and whose height dependence is a published closed form rather than a search? And if the answer must be recomputed at sea by every bird on every tick, what is the passage plan's actual cost, and what happens on the day the survey is superseded?
distance_rationale: Nothing about pilotage is simulation engineering, game rendering, or GIS software, and it predates all three by centuries — yet it is a mature discipline whose entire subject is the question this sitting is stuck on: how an agent with a fixed viewpoint, moving continuously, answers 'what can I see from here, and how far' cheaply enough to act on in real time, over an area far larger than anything it could survey itself. The craft solved it by moving the computation off the observer and into a published artefact, by reducing the height dependence to one closed form, by screening the SOURCE so the answer arrives pre-classified, and by attaching a survey date to everything so a stale authority is visible as stale. Those are exactly the four moves the sitting has not considered: it has drafted three observer-side raster options and declined all three on budget, without questioning that the answer is a raster or that the observer computes it. The domain also carries a hard-won discipline about derived, dated data that maps directly onto an occlusion artefact baked from footprints — and a canonical failure (the correctly charted, century-stale bank) that is the same shape as this project's two recorded measurement bugs.
expected_isomorphisms: Sector light ↔ source-side precomputed angular occlusion: screening at the lantern is per-occluder precomputation, and 'which colour am I in' is a two-bit answer to a visibility query, the strongest available counter-proposal to the per-cell grid all three declined options assume.

Dipping distance (≈ 2.08√h) ↔ altitude as a monotone closed-form range function, against the sitting's measured 5 m → 300 m curve that never saturates; the Light List's tabulated form is the integer, determinism-safe implementation of it.

Light List / pilot book edition + survey date + Notice to Mariners ↔ versioning and invalidation of an occlusion artefact derived from build_dsm.py, and whether that version enters the world identity hash and the replay fixture.
Chart datum and the ambiguous printed zero ↔ the DSM's nodata = 0 over 69.6% of its window, and whether 'unsurveyed' is distinguishable from 'open' in the sim's representation.

Transit / leading line ↔ an exact visibility predicate obtained by comparison rather than computation; clearing bearing ↔ the monotone 'is ward w readable from (p, h)' inequality, which is far cheaper than the visible-set answer the mechanic may not need.

Conspicuous-object doctrine (a sparse charted mark set) ↔ the 70 vantage sites, either rehabilitated as marks with a height and an arc or exposed as the fly-to-a-marker pattern returning under a new name.

Grounding on a correctly charted, century-stale bank ↔ the project's two recorded measurement bugs and the family they belong to: an artefact that looks like a measurement because nothing carries its provenance forward.
focus: Owns WHERE the visibility answer is precomputed and what a single query is allowed to cost. Specifically: whether occlusion should be precomputed observer-side (a per-cell grid, which is what all three declined options assume) or source-side (per-building or per-cluster angular arcs, the way a screened lantern partitions the water around it); whether altitude enters as a closed-form monotone range function r(h) rather than as a raster lookup; the per-query cost at dispatch time and the BYTE SIZE of what one observation writes into the fog's permanent Contents layer; and the edition/survey-date/invalidation discipline of any artefact derived from build_dsm.py — including whether that artefact's version participates in the identity hash. Also owns the DSM's nodata = 0 as a datum ambiguity, and whether the 70 vantage sites survive as charted marks carrying a real height and a real arc.
name: fd-pilotage-arc-and-range
persona: Apply the perspective of a licensed coastal pilot working a single district, together with the hydrographic office that supplies them — the civil craft of taking a hull through inshore water on PUBLISHED information rather than on-the-spot computation. This craft reasons about: the Light List and the pilot book (and their ancestors, the Mediterranean portolano and the northern rutter) as precomputed, dated, editioned tables that every navigator reads identically; the SECTOR LIGHT, whose lantern is screened at the source so the light itself partitions the surrounding water into named angular sectors — the mariner's entire visibility query collapses to 'which colour am I seeing', an O(1) categorical answer with no geometry performed at sea; the arc of visibility and the charted obscured sector, stated as bearing ranges seen FROM seaward; geographic range as a closed form in height alone (the dipping distance, ≈ 2.08(√H_eye + √H_light) nautical miles), tabulated once and read forever, and capped against luminous range; the TRANSIT or leading line — two marks brought into line yielding an exact position line with no instrument, no arithmetic and no error term; the CLEARING BEARING, which states a danger as an inequality on a bearing ('keep the tower open of the point') rather than as a shape to be computed; the rising-and-dipping method, which turns the instant a light first appears into a range fix; the chart's 'conspicuous object' symbol, the deliberately sparse hand-picked set of marks a pilot actually works from out of everything technically visible; chart datum and the drying height, where a printed zero means one thing to the surveyor and another to the keel; the Notice to Mariners cycle, the source-data diagram, and the survey date printed on every panel; the licensing of pilots per district, because the useful representation is local and does not generalise; and the trade's standing catastrophe — a competent navigator running hard aground on a bank that was exactly where the chart said, because the chart was surveyed by lead line a century ago and nothing in the passage plan carried its age.
review_areas: Observer-side versus source-side precomputation — every one of the three declined options (A decouple, B widen both, C shrink) precomputes at the OBSERVER's cell, and nothing in the sitting examines that premise. A screened lantern inverts it: visibility is computed once at the mark and published as an angular arc plus a height, and the query becomes 'is p inside mark m's obscured arc, given h'. Judge the object-count arithmetic honestly in both directions (49M cells at 4 m citywide versus 1.08M building polygons, and how many of those polygons can ever be horizon-defining for a given ward), and say which side of the query the storage should live on.

Altitude as a published closed form rather than a lookup — dipping distance is a √h table, not a computation. The sitting's own measurement (5 m → 300 m, 6,076 → 32,273 visible cells, 5.3×, monotone and never saturating) is a range curve waiting to be fitted. Test whether the entire altitude effect can be an integer monotone r(h) in metres or Bp plus a small per-ward correction, and whether that per-ward correction is exactly the 'different information economies' finding (BK02 9.9% at 5 m against MN01 0.5%, MN01 still worst at 300 m). If so, the citywide authority is ~71 numbers and one curve, not 49M cells — state whether that is enough for the mechanic or where it visibly breaks.

The cost of one query, the size of one answer, and whether the mechanic needs a SET at all — sector colour is O(1) and fits in two bits, and a clearing bearing states a danger as an inequality rather than as a region to be computed. Price each candidate structure at dispatch time: how many 'what can I see from (p, h)' queries per tick per bird at the shipped cadence, what each costs in integer operations, and how many BYTES one observation writes into the fog's permanent Contents layer over a 52-week year. Then ask the prior question: does the mechanic need a set of visible things, or only a monotone predicate ('is ward w readable from (p, h)?') resolvable against one precomputed per-(observer-cell, ward) threshold? The sitting measured that altitude changes how MUCH far more than WHICH — 'which' is the cheap inequality and 'how much' is the expensive set, and call 1 picked the expensive one without pricing the asymmetry.

Editions, survey dates and Notices to Mariners — any precomputed visibility artefact is a derived product of footprints' height_roof_m through build_dsm.py, so it has a survey date, a provenance chain and an invalidation rule, and the design states none of the three. Determine whether the artefact carries a version or content hash, whether that hash participates in the world identity hash (identity.rs) and therefore in replay locking (crates/raven-vocab/tests/fixtures/neutral_replay_1400.json), and what the stated procedure is when the bbox widens or city-sim's ward set changes. An unversioned derived authority silently changes what birds know on every re-bake.

The nodata = 0 datum ambiguity — the shipped DSM is float32 with nodata = 0 and carries surface on only 30.4% of its own 3584 × 4456 window, while ground is treated as z = 0 because Lower Manhattan is nearly flat. That is a printed zero meaning two different things (no survey here versus surface at datum), which is the chart-datum failure exactly. Judge what any candidate structure does at the 69.6% of cells with no data, whether 'unsurveyed' is distinguishable from 'open sky' in the sim's representation, and whether the withdrawn MN01 canyon reading and the confounded ward-count finding both trace to this same undeclared zero.

Conspicuous objects and whether z deletes the vantage site — pilotage works from a deliberately sparse set of charted marks, each with a height, an arc, and a name, not from everything visible. Assess whether that rehabilitates the 70 placeholder vantage sites as real marks (a height, an arc of visibility, a range) rather than deleting them as the ruling assumes — and be adversarial in both directions, because a sparse named mark set is also precisely how 'fly to a marker and press the button' comes back wearing a new hat. State which reading the fog mechanic's two layers actually support.
severity_examples: P0: the sim's occlusion authority is defined as a derived product of the renderer's bake with no independent edition, survey date, or content hash — one source, two budgets, no version on either. Every re-bake or bbox widening then silently changes what every bird knows, the world identity hash moves for a reason nothing records, and neutral_replay_1400.json re-locks with no recoverable explanation. This is not a tuning problem later; a replayable engine whose perception authority is an unversioned derived artefact is not replayable, and the fix is a pipeline and hashing change that has to precede any occlusion code.

P1: no candidate structure is priced per query at dispatch time and no candidate states the bytes one observation writes into the permanent Contents layer. The scout economy is already at its edge — every-3-weeks is the only viable cadence and the scout's food floor is exactly 0 — so a perception query whose cost scales with what it reveals will be discovered only after the cadence is retuned around it, and the retune will read as a balance decision rather than as the structural cost it is.

P2: the DSM's nodata = 0 is carried into the sim unchanged, so 'no surface surveyed' and 'surface at ground datum' are the same value. Wards outside the 30.4% survived window read as perfectly open sky rather than as unknown, which is the same shape as the two recorded measurement bugs — a value that looks like a measurement and is an artefact of the container.
source_domain: Coastal pilotage and the sea-mark system — the civil hydrographic craft of moving a hull through inshore water on published, dated, editioned information rather than on-the-spot computation. Its working apparatus: the Light List and pilot book (portolano, rutter) as precomputed tables; the sector light, which screens the source so the mark itself partitions surrounding space into named angular sectors and the observer's query becomes O(1) categorical; the charted arc of visibility and obscured sector; geographic range as a closed form in height alone (dipping distance ≈ 2.08(√H_eye + √H_light) nm), capped by luminous range; the transit or leading line as an exact position line requiring no instrument; the clearing bearing, which states danger as an inequality rather than a region; rising-and-dipping as a range fix; the sparse 'conspicuous object' mark set; chart datum and drying heights, where a printed zero is ambiguous by construction; the Notice to Mariners cycle, source-data diagram and per-panel survey date; district-limited pilot licensing because the useful representation does not generalise; and the trade's standing catastrophe — grounding on a correctly charted bank whose survey was a century stale and whose age travelled with nothing.
success_hints: Do the arithmetic in the finding. Recompute the citywide cell counts at 1/2/4/8/16/32 m and put the source-side alternative beside them: 1.08M building polygons, and the far smaller count of polygons that can be horizon-defining for any given ward once a height threshold is applied (the p90 is 36.9 m and the max is 429.3 m — most buildings can never define a skyline for a bird above 40 m). A finding that says 'cheaper' without a number is not usable here.

Read pipeline/scripts/build_dsm.py for MergeAlg.max, the nodata convention and the CRS (EPSG:32618), and pipeline/scripts/nyc_bbox.py for BBOX_WGS84 — the sitting claims widening is one edit and a re-run, and that claim is checkable. Note whether the rasterization is deterministic across GDAL versions, because a derived authority that depends on a library version is a survey with no date.

Read crates/animal-sim/src/fixed.rs first and list which integer operations actually exist (Bp clamp semantics, saturating add, mul_bp, what the u16 range costs in precision at city scale). Judge each proposed closed form against that list rather than against 'fixed-point is possible in principle' — √h and any trigonometry need an explicit integer construction, and a table is usually the honest one.

Trace one query end to end in crates/animal-sim/src/dispatch.rs and sites.rs: where would a visibility test be called from, how often per tick, and what does the caller do with the answer? The shape of the CALLER constrains the representation more than the storage budget does, and the caller is already written.

Check what the fog leg actually stores per observation today (the Contents/State two-layer model, the week timestamp, the 453bp divergence metric) before proposing what a spatial fog would store — the permanent layer is the one that grows without bound over a 52-week year, and it is the layer the sitting's ruling changes from per-ward to spatial.
task_context: Read docs/design-2026-07-31-playable-middle.md section 'Sitting L — the z-axis' FIRST; it carries every measurement and both measurement bugs, and it is the context for this whole review. THE QUESTION: how should RaveNous represent and query citywide building-height/occlusion so the SIMULATION can cheaply and DETERMINISTICALLY answer 'what can a bird at altitude h over point p see?' — and what options exist beyond the three drafted and declined there (decouple sim grid from render bake / widen both / shrink to seven wards)? Draw hard on GIS practice, not just game-engine practice: precomputed visibility structures (sky view factor, cumulative and total viewshed indices, visibility graphs, potentially-visible sets), horizon and skyline angular representations per cell or per perch, analytic visibility straight from footprint polygons with no raster at all, isovists and space syntax, multi-resolution pyramids and quadtrees, cloud-optimized and tiled raster access, quantized-mesh and terrain LOD, 3D Tiles and CityGML LOD, XDraw and reference-plane approximate viewsheds, R2/R3, GPU depth-buffer and cubemap methods. DETERMINISM IS NON-NEGOTIABLE: the engine is hash-identity replayable and fixed-point throughout (Bp = u16 basis points, BP_ONE = 10000), animal-sim is vocabulary-agnostic under ruling R12 and gated by scripts/check-agnosticism.sh, and city-sim is a READ-ONLY cross-repo path dep at ../infinite-fun-space-app/crates/city-sim that must not be modified. So: which methods admit integer or fixed-point implementations; is a small precomputed per-cell scalar enough or does the mechanic need a real per-query viewshed; is there a representation where the ANSWER stays small even though the city is big; does any of it let the vantage site (the 70 placeholder sites all pinned at pos_bp (5000,5000), one per non-home ward) survive in a better form, or does z delete it. Be adversarial about the sitting's own call-1 ruling that 'altitude is the fog's currency', given the measurement that altitude changes how MUCH of a ward you see far more than WHICH wards you see. Also weigh the pipeline fact that build_dsm.py rasterizes the footprints' OWN height_roof_m, so the sim's occlusion grid and the renderer's building bake are two artefacts derived from one source with wildly different budgets (98 MB at 4 m citywide uint16 vs 1.08M buildings the renderer cannot draw). Judge design consequences too, not just data structures: what does height do to the fog mechanic, to dispatch, to the pause tier, and to R12 agnosticism. Material to read beyond the sitting: docs/design-2026-07-31-playable-middle.md § 'Ruling — all wards, under fog (GATE 1)' for the two-layer fog model (Contents permanent / State perishable, timestamped) and for Tier::Pause's stated trigger (belief↔truth divergence); § 'Measured — the fog leg' for the shipped scout economy (every-3-weeks is the only viable cadence, 18 scout returns a year, 19/71 wards known at week 52, mean staleness 24 weeks, mean divergence 453bp); crates/animal-sim/src/fixed.rs (Bp, BP_ONE = 10_000, clamp/saturating/mul_bp — the whole integer vocabulary available); crates/animal-sim/src/world.rs (Site, Region, pos_bp, entry_pos_bp), sites.rs (distance_bp), dispatch.rs, identity.rs; scripts/check-agnosticism.sh (its RAVEN_WORDS ban-list is the R12 gate any new name must pass); pipeline/scripts/build_dsm.py and nyc_bbox.py; crates/raven-vocab/tests/fixtures/neutral_replay_1400.json (what re-locks if the identity hash moves). city-sim at ../infinite-fun-space-app/crates/city-sim is READ-ONLY — findings may depend on what it exposes but may not propose editing it. Severity: P0 = would corrupt or block the whole design; P1 = must fix before implementing; P2 = degrades quality; P3 = polish. Ground every storage or cost claim in arithmetic done in the finding, not in adjectives. This lens reads the question as a hydrographic-publication question: not 'what can be seen' but 'what has been surveyed, published, dated, and reduced to something a working navigator resolves in one look'. Give particular weight to inverting the query (precompute at the occluder, not at the observer), to altitude as a closed-form range rather than a lookup, to the per-query and per-answer cost at dispatch time, and to the edition/invalidation discipline of an artefact derived from build_dsm.py. Where a finding depends on a storage or cost claim, compute the number in the finding.
